# districtry

> Click a point, or type an address, and see every civic district that covers it — and who holds those seats. Ten instances across Illinois, New York, San Francisco, Wisconsin, Iowa, Michigan, Minnesota, Kentucky, Indiana and North Carolina. Every boundary and every name comes from a published source and is cited to it.

Free, no account, no tracking of individuals. The map runs in the browser; what each page sends to whom is listed at https://districtry.com/privacy.html.

## The whole site

- [districtry](https://districtry.com/): the front door. Type an address and it opens whichever instance covers it, with the point already selected; a point nobody covers is told so rather than routed somewhere wrong.
- [Privacy](https://districtry.com/privacy.html)
- [Sponsorship](https://districtry.com/sponsorship.html)
- [Traffic report](https://districtry.com/traffic.html)
- [About districtry](https://districtry.com/about.html)
- [How districtry uses AI](https://districtry.com/ai.html)
- [Report a problem or leave a comment](https://districtry.com/feedback.html)

## Illinois

93 counties. Wards, county boards, police districts and beats, school zones, judicial subcircuits, and the people who hold those seats.

- [Illinois district lookup](https://districtry.com/il/): 41 layers, 93 counties.
- [Who is my U.S. representative?](https://districtry.com/il/congress.html)
- [Who is my county commissioner?](https://districtry.com/il/county-board.html): links a page per county, 94 of them, each naming every member with whatever contact details that county publishes.
- [Who runs my fire protection district?](https://districtry.com/il/fire-district.html)
- [What judicial subcircuit am I in?](https://districtry.com/il/judicial-subcircuit.html)
- [Who runs my library district?](https://districtry.com/il/library-district.html)
- [Who runs my park district?](https://districtry.com/il/park-district.html)
- [What Chicago police district am I in?](https://districtry.com/il/police-district.html)
- [Which counties publish precinct maps?](https://districtry.com/il/precinct-maps.html)
- [What voting precinct am I in? Illinois](https://districtry.com/il/precinct.html)
- [Which CPS school board district am I in?](https://districtry.com/il/school-board.html)
- [Sources & data layers](https://districtry.com/il/sources.html)
- [Who is my Illinois state legislator?](https://districtry.com/il/state-legislature.html)
- [Who is my Supreme Court justice?](https://districtry.com/il/supreme-court.html)
- [What township am I in?](https://districtry.com/il/township.html)
- [Who is my alderman? Chicago wards](https://districtry.com/il/ward.html)
- [Chicago district questions](https://districtry.com/il/faq.html)
- [History](https://districtry.com/il/history.html)

- [What community board am I in?](https://districtry.com/ny/community-board.html)
- [Who is my U.S. representative?](https://districtry.com/ny/congress.html)
- [What Council district am I in?](https://districtry.com/ny/council-district.html)
- [Who is my county legislator?](https://districtry.com/ny/county-legislature.html): links a page per county, 1 of them, each naming every member with whatever contact details that county publishes.
- [Who is my county supervisor?](https://districtry.com/ny/county-supervisor.html): links a page per county, 4 of them, each naming every member with whatever contact details that county publishes.
- [What NYPD precinct am I in?](https://districtry.com/ny/police-precinct.html)
- [Sources & data layers](https://districtry.com/ny/sources.html)

## Michigan

All 83 counties: commissioner districts, compiled by the state from the plan each county's apportionment commission files — plus townships and charter townships, cities and villages, school districts and intermediate school districts, circuit courts and Court of Appeals districts, and the Michigan Senate, House and U.S. House seats, and who holds those.

- [Michigan district lookup](https://districtry.com/mi/): 19 layers, all 83 counties.
- [Who is on my city council?](https://districtry.com/mi/city-council.html)
- [Who is my U.S. representative?](https://districtry.com/mi/congress.html)
- [County commissioner district lookup](https://districtry.com/mi/county-commissioner.html): links a page per county, 83 of them, each naming every member with whatever contact details that county publishes.
- [Sources & data layers](https://districtry.com/mi/sources.html)
- [Who is my Michigan legislator?](https://districtry.com/mi/state-legislature.html)
- [Michigan district questions](https://districtry.com/mi/faq.html)
- [History](https://districtry.com/mi/history.html)

## Minnesota

All 87 counties: county board districts in every one of them, judicial districts, townships and cities, school districts, ZIP codes, and the nearest police station, fire station and post office — plus the Minnesota Senate, House and U.S. House districts, and who holds the U.S. House seats. Nobody is named yet on the county boards, the judges' benches or the two state chambers, and the Data gaps panel says why.

- [Minnesota district lookup](https://districtry.com/mn/): 18 layers, all 87 counties.
- [Who is my U.S. representative?](https://districtry.com/mn/congress.html)
- [County commissioner district lookup](https://districtry.com/mn/county-commissioner.html): links a page per county, 87 of them, each naming every member with whatever contact details that county publishes.
- [Sources & data layers](https://districtry.com/mn/sources.html)

## Kentucky

All 120 counties: the county a point sits in, and the Kentucky Senate, House and U.S. House districts — with the member named for each U.S. House seat. Nobody is named yet on the two state chambers or the fiscal courts, and the Data gaps panel says why.

- [Kentucky district lookup](https://districtry.com/ky/): 12 layers, all 120 counties.
- [Who is my U.S. representative?](https://districtry.com/ky/congress.html)
- [Sources & data layers](https://districtry.com/ky/sources.html)
- [Kentucky district questions](https://districtry.com/ky/faq.html)

## Indiana

All 92 counties: townships, cities and towns, school districts, ZIP codes, and the nearest police station, fire station and post office — plus the Indiana Senate, House and U.S. House districts, with the member named for each U.S. House seat. Nobody is named yet on the two state chambers or the county governments, and the Data gaps panel says why.

- [Indiana district lookup](https://districtry.com/in/): 11 layers, all 92 counties.
- [Who is my U.S. representative?](https://districtry.com/in/congress.html)
- [Who are my county commissioners?](https://districtry.com/in/county-commissioner.html): links a page per county, 91 of them, each naming every member with whatever contact details that county publishes.
- [Sources & data layers](https://districtry.com/in/sources.html)
- [Indiana district questions](https://districtry.com/in/faq.html)

## North Carolina

All 100 counties: townships, cities and towns, school districts, ZIP codes, and the nearest police station, fire station and post office — plus the North Carolina Senate, House and U.S. House districts, with the member named for every seat. Nobody is named yet on the county boards or city councils, and the Data gaps panel says why.

- [North Carolina district lookup](https://districtry.com/nc/): 11 layers, all 100 counties.
- [Who is my U.S. representative?](https://districtry.com/nc/congress.html)
- [Sources & data layers](https://districtry.com/nc/sources.html)
- [Who is my NC legislator?](https://districtry.com/nc/state-legislature.html)

## Where the answers come from

Each instance's sources page carries one row per layer: what it answers, the publisher its boundary comes from, where the names on its card come from, and the ground it answers on. That page is generated from the same list that registers the layers, so a layer cannot ship without a row.

Officeholder names are never guessed. Where no verifiable roster exists, a card links the official body instead of inventing a name, and what the project does not know is recorded rather than left blank — each instance ships a machine-readable list of its own gaps at `<instance>/data/app/coverage-gaps.json`.

Sources last reverified between October 9, 2026 and September 30, 2026, per instance.

This is a civic reference tool and it disclaims legal precision. Confirm a district assignment with the government office that draws it before relying on it for anything official.

## Terms

`https://districtry.com/robots.txt` publishes a Content-Signal, and these are the values in it: ai-input=yes, ai-train=no, search=yes, use=reference.

In plain words: indexing and search are welcome, and so is grounding an answer in these pages, on the terms the signal names — by reference, with a link back to the page that names the person, so a reader can check the government source behind it. Training is reserved. No crawler is disallowed by name: a site that wants its answers found does not gain anything by refusing the clients that find them.

The boundaries and rosters are public records from the publishers each sources page names; this project's own work is the collection, the citation and the code.

Corrections: corrections@overberg.co. Source: https://github.com/ThursdaysFamous/districtry
